# Case 1: 3 nodes with simple distances
{"knnIdx":  [[1,2],[0,2],[0,1]], "knnDist": [[0.5,2.0],[0.5,1.5],[2.0,1.5]],"rho":[0.5,0.5,1.5],"sigma":[1.0,1.0,1.0]}
@ Expected p_{j|i} for each directed edge
[[0,1,1.0],[0,2,0.22313016],[1,0,1.0],[1,2,0.36787944],[2,0,0.60653066],[2,1,1.0]]

# Case 2: 2 nodes, symmetric distances, rho=0, sigma=1
{"knnIdx":[[1],[0]],"knnDist":[[1.0],[1.0]],"rho":[0,0],"sigma":[1.0,1.0]}
@ p = exp(-1) in both directions
[[0,1,0.36787944],[1,0,0.36787944]]

# Case 3: 3 nodes in a line, sigma=2 for all
{"knnIdx":[[1],[0,2],[1]],"knnDist":[[1.0],[1.0,1.0],[1.0]],"rho":[0,0,0],"sigma":[2.0,2.0,2.0]}
@ p = exp(-0.5) between adjacent nodes
[[0,1,0.60653066],[1,0,0.60653066],[1,2,0.60653066],[2,1,0.60653066]]

# Case 4: 3 nodes, non-zero rho
{"knnIdx":[[1,2],[0],[0]],"knnDist":[[0.5,2.5],[0.5],[2.5]],"rho":[0.5,0.5,2.5],"sigma":[1.0,1.0,1.0]}
@ p01=1, p02=exp(-2), p10=1, p20=1
[[0,1,1.0],[0,2,0.13533528],[1,0,1.0],[2,0,1.0]]

# Case 5: 2 nodes with different sigmas
{"knnIdx":[[1],[0]],"knnDist":[[2.0],[2.0]],"rho":[0,0],"sigma":[0.5,2.0]}
@ p01=exp(-4), p10=exp(-1)
